title: Drywall Patch
short_answer: Patching is judgment work. Picking the right method for the size of the hole is most of the job.
summary: Small hole, one method. Big hole, a different one. Spread the mud out much wider than you think you need to and feather it to nothing.
plain_words: Small hole, one method. Big hole, a different one. Then spread the mud out much wider than you think you need to and feather it to nothing. Patches show because the mud stopped too soon, not because the hole was too big.
when_to_use: Repair holes from fist-size down to nail pops
Medium and large openings needing backing
Rated wall breaches — full assembly restoration only
prerequisites: Know what is behind the wall before cutting (wiring, plumbing, conduit)
Rated assembly identified before any breach repair

steps.title: Nail pops and dings
steps.body: Set or replace the fastener, then two to three thin coats, each wider than the last. No tape needed unless the paper is broken.

steps.title: Small holes (butterfly)
steps.body: California / butterfly patch: scrap 3–4" larger than the hole, score back 1½–2" in, leave face paper as flange, butter, set, squeeze excess from under flange, coat out wider each pass.

steps.title: Square the hole
steps.body: Square up the hole and cut back to sound board before butterfly or backed patch.

steps.title: Check before cutting
steps.body: Check for wiring, plumbing, and conduit before cutting. Always, no exceptions.

steps.title: Backed patch
steps.body: Cut to a clean rectangle, install backing screwed through existing board, fit piece with small gap, screw to backing, tape all four sides, coat in progressively wider passes.

steps.title: Match thickness
steps.body: Match the existing board thickness. A patch sitting proud or low cannot be hidden.

steps.title: Setting compound
steps.body: Setting compound for fill coats — same-day recoats. Clean tools before it sets.

steps.title: Final coat
steps.body: Topping or lightweight for the final coat even if fills were hot mud — the last coat is the one you sand.

steps.title: Batch the work
steps.body: Walk the area, mark every patch, then all cut-outs, all fills, all coats — same logic as production framing.

steps.title: Feather wide
steps.body: Feather wider than feels necessary. This is the difference between an invisible patch and a callback.

steps.title: Sand and texture
steps.body: Sand smooth with raking light. Match surrounding texture before paint.

steps.title: Prime
steps.body: Prime the patch. Bare compound absorbs paint differently — the #1 cause of a repair showing through.

steps.title: Photo T&M
steps.body: Photograph before and after, room identified. On T&M work that is the backup for the ticket.

warnings.title: Why we work this way
warnings.body: The patch fails at its edges, not in its middle. Almost every visible patch is visible because the mud was feathered over too small an area.

warnings.title: Rated walls and smoke barriers
warnings.body: A hole in a fire-rated wall is a breach of a tested assembly — a cosmetic patch does not restore it. Repair with the same board type and thickness, same layers, same fastener pattern, and specified joint treatment. Penetrations get the listed firestop system. If you do not know the assembly, stop and find out.

experts.summary: Nail pops/dings: reset fastener, thin coats wider each pass. Small (up to fist-size): California/butterfly — paper flange is the tape, squeeze trapped mud out or it bubbles later. Medium/large: clean square, backing, tape four sides, coat out. Very large / rated: cut to framing and restore full listed assembly — reconstruction, not patching.

variations.title: California / butterfly patch
variations.when: Small holes up to about fist-size
changes: Scrap 3–4" larger than hole both ways
Score back 1½–2" from each edge; snap gypsum, leave face paper flange
Butter hole, set plug, press flange, squeeze excess mud out
Coat over whole flange, each coat wider, then feather

variations.title: Rated assembly repair
changes: Same board type, thickness, layer count, fastener pattern
Specified joint treatment and listed firestop at penetrations
Stop if assembly is unknown — life safety

quality_checks.prompt: Method matches hole size (butterfly vs backed vs full assembly)
Mud feathered wide — edges invisible in raking light
Rated breaches restored per listed assembly — not cosmetic only

common_mistakes.title: Feather too small
common_mistakes.wrong: Small thick bump at the repair edge
common_mistakes.why: Visible halo is the #1 patch callback

common_mistakes.title: Trapped mud under butterfly flange
common_mistakes.right: Squeeze excess out with knife before coating

common_mistakes.title: Cosmetic rated repair
common_mistakes.wrong: Mud over a rated breach without restoring assembly
common_mistakes.right: Full listed assembly or stop for engineering

troubleshooting.fix: Cut out blistered section, re-bed flange, squeeze excess out
Skim wider with topping; re-check in raking light

next_steps.label: Paint Touch-Up
next_steps.why: After prime — same product, same tool, recoat the plane

next_steps.label: QC Walk
next_steps.why: Raking light before calling patch done

provenance.note: California/butterfly patch dimensions (scrap 3–4" oversize with 1½–2" paper flange) are standard published method. Setting-compound behavior follows manufacturer guidance. Rated-assembly repair requirements come from the listing for the specific assembly.
